faq.a: Amadou is associated with the Arabic form أَحْمَدُو, whose core sense is amadou; ahmad (west african form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Amadou?
faq.a: Amadou is associated with Arabic. Amadou is the West African (Fulani/Wolof) form of Arabic أَحْمَد (Aḥmad), meaning 'most praiseworthy'.
Yes — the underlying form أَحْمَدُو is Arabic.
Amadou can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Amadou should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Aḥmad is a Quranic Arabic form and occurs in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Amadou mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Amadou is rendered احمدو and carries the sense احمدو، احمد.

faq.q: What does Amadou mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Amadou is rendered احمدو and carries the sense احمدو، احمد.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-ma-dou. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Amadou?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Amadou, amadou. Script forms are أَحْمَدُو, احمدو, अमादु.

faq.q: Is Amadou a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
